newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA INDUSTRIALS END WEAK, GOLDS OFF ON BULLION.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA INDUSTRIALS END WEAK, GOLDS OFF ON BULLION.

text.p: South African shares ended slightly weaker in quiet trade as the rand moved off firmer early levels. Gold shares closed weak on a softer bullion price.
"The market ended firm but it was not convincing. When the market opened everything looked positive except for the gold price," a dealer said.

Dealers said the market opened slightly firm on the rand and ticked up at noon on the back of stronger world markets. As the rand slipped off morning highs in the afternoon industrials also moved lower.
"It has been a topsy-turvy day," one dealer said.
Volumes traded were high and dealers said there had been good two-way trade. Institutions were absent and futures players helped push volumes higher, they said.

Dealers said the market would take its cue from Wall Street on Monday. The local consumer inflation index -- due Wednesday -- would be watched for further direction, but the currency would be the main indicator of the direction of the market.
The overall index ended down 3.8 points to 7,003.8 points, industrial index gained 6.3 points to 8,258.4 points and golds fell 15.1 points to 1,668.4 points.
De Beers was up 25 cents to 144.75 rand, Anglo lost 50 cents to 292.75 rand and SA Breweries slipped 50 cents to 122.50 rand.
Vaal Reefs shed 250 cents to 372.50 rand, Freegold dropped 50 cents to 40.50 rand and Dries was off 25 cents to 53.75 rand.
Near-term industrial equity futures ended weak, depressed by a weaker rand at close. Gold contracts were soft on negative sentiment from bullion failing to test upper levels.
The market was seen looking to Wall Street next week for direction and the CPI figure due on Wednesday.
December all-share contract offered at 6,490/570 from 6,535, gold contract at 1,195/210 from 1,215 and industrial contract at 8,000/17 from 8,050.
